author: TEDx Talks
description:
We've been told the future of AI looks like ever-bigger data centers — warehouses that drink a town's water and draw a city's power so the same two chatbots can answer everyone's questions. Dimitrios Nikolopoulos, who has spent 30 years in high-performance computing, thinks that future is both unnecessary and a dead end. His provocation: the leaps in computing have almost never come from making machines bigger. They've come from making them smaller. An iPhone 7 outran the fastest supercomputer of 1995. A game console beats the one that topped the year 2000.

Follow that curve forward and the picture flips. Instead of intelligence locked inside a handful of remote, resource-hungry mega-centers, it could live on small, capable devices — the kind you could put in a home, a school, or a business. And that's not a downgrade; it's a more resilient, more private, more sustainable, and more personal way to compute, and it's exactly what his lab is building.

title: Why more AI data centers aren’t the answer | Dimitrios Nikolopoulos | TEDxMidAtlantic

Tyler texted this to Jami before the show - Jami still trying to clarify with Tyler 9-20-2026: What can surfing teach us about cancer?
Tyler Callaway is a lifelong surfer and multi-time cancer survivor whose colorful life has taken him from championship surfing and the surf industry to entrepreneurship, invention, philanthropy—and some experiences that sound almost impossible.
He was bitten by a shark in the morning, struck by lightning that same afternoon, and somehow walked away from both.

Prema Walker, Founder and CEO of Prema’s Permaculture & Composting, outlines a durable model for local social entrepreneurship based on California's organic waste diversion law. She details how her proof-of-concept urban farm has successfully diverted over 700,000 pounds of organic waste from landfills to model micro-scale agricultural sustainability. Prema Walker is the Founder and CEO of Prema's Permaculture & Composting in the Coachella Valley. She grew up in India watching her grandfather farm land he had worked his entire life without ever building lasting financial security from it. When she settled in the Coachella Valley in 2020, she saw the same story among local growers, and it became one of the reasons she built her business.

title: From food waste to food abundance | Prema Walker | TEDxRancho Mirage

description: Oxford-trained Clinical Psychologist Dr. Romi Ran discusses moving past traditional psychological frameworks to explore the core of human identity. Drawing from years of intensive contemplative practices, including extended solitary and darkroom retreats, she explains what it means to strip away societal identity and experience life more directly. Dr. Romi Ran is an Oxford-trained Clinical Psychologist, speaker, and author whose work explores the relationship between the mind, suffering, and human experience. After more than a decade working within traditional psychological frameworks, she became increasingly interested in the deeper mechanisms underlying thought, perception, and identity. Her perspective has been deeply shaped by several years of intensive contemplative practice, including extended solitary and dark room retreats, which continue to inform her clinical work. Her TEDx talk challenges the way we understand our own experience and explores what it means to experience life
title: What you're experiencing is not what's happening | Dr. Romi Ran | TEDxRancho Mirage

description: Ultramarathon athlete Ivan Borzenko shares his journey from a childhood prognosis that he might spend his life in a wheelchair to completing a 320-mile triathlon and serving on an emergency medical team on Mt. Everest. His talk explores the invisible barriers society constructs around potential and challenges audiences to look beyond their perceived limits. Ivan was once told he may never walk and could spend his life in a wheelchair. Years later, he would go on to pursue a Guinness World Record during a 320-mile triathlon and serve with an emergency medical team on Mt. Everest. Through his story, Ivan explores the invisible barriers society builds around possibility and the ways those limits shape how people see themselves. Whether someone is facing challenges in their career, family, health, or personal goals, this is a reminder that our perceived limits are often much smaller than our true potential. title: Limits are learned, not biologically fixed | Ivan Borzenko | TEDxRancho Mirage

Anastassiya Savchenko, founder of Nutcrackers Creative Agency and the Indian Women Impact, is a social educator committed to empowering children and amplifying unheard voices. She spoke about the “business of compassion,” reminding us that meaningful impact can begin with something as simple as helping a child find their voice or reminding them that they matter. Many children miss school not because they lack potential, but because circumstances and responsibilities hold them back. She has helped children from daily-wage families discover their passions and become ballet dancers, MUN competitors, singers, and chess players. Anastassiya showed us that compassion means showing up, changing the odds, and empowering others to shape their own futures.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this thought-provoking TEDx Talk, the speaker introduces a powerful idea: The Human Ledger—the invisible record of the people who believed in us, worked with us, trusted us, and whose lives were changed because of the businesses we built.

Drawing from a journey that began with a modest farming background, the speaker shares how his entrepreneurial success was shaped not merely by financial capital, but by trust, relationships, mentorship, responsibility, and human belief.

From choosing business partners to hiring employees, every decision creates an entry in our human ledger. And when a devastating fire destroyed his company’s physical infrastructure, that ledger became more important than ever. Buildings and equipment could be rebuilt—but protecting the people, their dignity, and their trust was the real priority.

The talk challenges us to rethink how we define business success.

Financial numbers tell us what we have built.
The Human Ledger tells us whom we have impacted.

So,
title: What if your business had a balance sheet that measured more than money? | Kirit Joshi | TEDxSCES

How do we truly ignite ourselves as members of youth in society? Annie Wu takes us on her journey from rejection to D1 golfer to one of the top university teams in America.  My name is Annie Wu, and I’m a Division I student-athlete, captain of Elon University’s women’s golf team, and is about to pursue a master’s degree at Boston University. While I’m honored to have earned Team MVP and Conference Player of the Week awards, my journey in junior golf wasn’t as glamorous as you’d imagine.
There was a time when the pressure, expectations, and uncertainty dimmed my hope for my American dream. I wasn’t sure if I could overcome difficulties, or if the passion I once had was still there. But that moment didn’t end my story, it ignited something deeper. It pushed me to another step, rebuild my confidence, and keep building on what I already have instead of giving up.
That spark, my passion, didn’t just come back; it came back stronger. It taught me that being ignited isn’t about always feelin
title: Protect the Spark | Annie Wu | TEDxHWIS Youth

In this talk, the speaker explores the struggle between motivation, distraction, and passion through relatable experiences with schoolwork, social media, and everyday procrastination. Moving beyond simple productivity advice, the talk examines how having a meaningful goal can create the motivation needed to take action, while genuine passion can help individuals resist external expectations and pursue paths that truly matter to them. Drawing on personal experiences and the pressures faced by many young people, particularly within Asian households, this talk encourages students to reflect on what drives them, challenge the limitations placed upon them, and find the courage to pursue goals of their own.
